name: @diagrid/n8n
description: Durable execution of n8n workflow node runs on Dapr Workflows
author: Diagrid Inc.
//peerDependenciesMeta: `optional: true` here is a pnpm-install-time workaround, not a real
statement that this package works without these five peers — it does
not. Without it, pnpm's autoInstallPeers tries to satisfy the bare `*`
peer range by fetching the REAL published n8n-nodes-base from npm (a
different, unrelated version from this workspace's own local n8n
checkout), which pulls in xlsx via a non-standard URL and trips this
repo's own blockExoticSubdeps supply-chain policy. `optional: true`
stops that auto-install attempt; the real, correct versions still come
from the sibling n8n checkout via scripts/link-n8n-dev-deps.sh.
//devDependencies: n8n-core/n8n-workflow/n8n-nodes-base/@n8n/db/@n8n/di are real peer
dependencies (see peerDependencies above) but are deliberately NOT listed
here as file: devDependencies pointing at the sibling n8n checkout: n8n's
own packages depend on ~20 further n8n-internal packages via workspace:*
(@n8n/backend-common, @n8n/config, n8n-workflow, ...), which only resolves
inside n8n's OWN pnpm workspace. Pointing a file: dependency at them from
this workspace makes pnpm try (and fail) to resolve those same specifiers
here, breaking `pnpm install` for the whole repo, not just this package.
See scripts/link-n8n-dev-deps.sh (in this package) and README.md's
'Developing against a local n8n checkout' section for how this
package's node_modules gets real
n8n type/runtime resolution instead: direct symlinks into
packages/n8n/node_modules, bypassing pnpm's own dependency graph for
exactly these five packages, the same way a real n8n install's own
node_modules is what actually satisfies these peers at runtime.
A real, PUBLISHED-npm-version devDependency (not a file: link) for
n8n-core/n8n-workflow/@n8n/db/@n8n/di specifically — the four peers this
package actually has a static `import` for, so typecheck (not runtime)
would work in a from-scratch checkout with no sibling n8n repo at all
(CI included) — was investigated and reverted, not just skipped. It
resolved and installed, but hit two real, separate problems: (1) their
own transitive dependencies (n8n-core's isolated-vm/ssh2/cpu-features,
Sentry's native profiler) trip pnpm's allowBuilds gate — workable, by
setting those `false` (declined, not silently ignored) rather than
expanding the workspace's real native-build-script surface just for
types; but then (2) pnpm resolves n8n-workflow into two STRUCTURALLY
DIFFERENT peer-hashed instances (n8n-core's own copy vs @n8n/db's own
copy) when these packages are installed as independent top-level
devDependencies outside n8n's own cohesive workspace — TypeScript then
sees e.g. `INode` from one instance as a different nominal type than
`INode` from the other, producing real 'not assignable' errors across
this package's own files that have nothing to do with an actual bug.
That is a structural consequence of installing n8n's own
tightly-interdependent packages outside n8n's own workspace, not
something a version pin or a pnpm override can safely paper over without
significant, fragile upkeep.
What actually resolves this for CI (and for anyone without a sibling
checkout) is scripts/ci-n8n-types.sh: a pinned, disposable n8n checkout
(n8n-ci-ref.txt), scoped-installed and scoped-built to just the closure
these four peers need, then symlinked in exactly like
link-n8n-dev-deps.sh does for a live one — never copied; a copy would
carry n8n-core's own internal symlink to n8n-workflow along with it and,
if dereferenced, reproduce the exact dual-instance problem above by a
different route. See README.md's 'CI has no sibling checkout of its
own' section for the full account, including why this is not a
substitute for a live checkout (it's read-only and pinned, not meant to
be developed against).
